recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中可見多個一端拉長成單一尾巴的淚滴狀紅血球（dacryocyte），並伴隨橢圓形紅血球與輕度大小不一，是原發性骨髓纖維化等骨髓浸潤疾病常見的抹片表現。
features: Several teardrop-shaped red cells (dacryocytes) with a single tapered tail
Accompanying elliptocytes and oval cells with moderate poikilocytosis
Mild anisocytosis with most cells normochromic and preserved central pallor
Occasional irregular fragment-like or folded red cells
Scattered small platelets; no nucleated red cells or leukocytes in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows moderate poikilocytosis with numerous teardrop cells (dacryocytes), elliptocytes, and occasional irregular red cell forms, with mild anisocytosis and normochromic cells. Platelets are present, and no nucleated red cells or immature myeloid cells are seen in this field. The teardrops are well spread in a thin area, so drying artifact is less likely because their tails point in different directions. Findings are consistent with dacryocytosis, as seen in primary myelofibrosis and other causes of marrow infiltration; review for leukoerythroblastosis and a bone marrow biopsy are recommended.

ddx.vs: Artifactual teardrops have tails all pointing in the same direction, whereas true dacryocytes are oriented randomly as here.

ddx.dx: Myelophthisis from metastatic tumor or granulomatous disease
ddx.vs: Myelophthisis produces identical teardrops with leukoerythroblastosis, and separation requires marrow biopsy rather than smear morphology.
Thalassemia shows microcytic hypochromic cells and target cells, and megaloblastic anemia shows oval macrocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, alongside teardrops.
